items.excerpt: A SubmitHub study found AI involvement detected in nearly 40% of music released in July, with almost a quarter fully AI-generated. It's the clearest data yet on how fast generative tools have entered everyday release workflows.

LANDR, Moises AI, Voice-Swap and more: a roundup of six AI music tools that license their training data and share revenue with the artists behind it. A practical guide for producers who want AI in the chain without the ethical debt.

Alibaba has launched HappyShrimp 1.0 in beta, an AI song generator whose prompts can specify instrumentation, vocal style and how a track's energy shifts across its running time. China's Taihe Music has signed up for artist co-creation.
Organismi OR—1 is a generative, stochastic MIDI pattern generator — free for iPad as an AUv3, €19.99 on macOS. A reminder that algorithmic composition tools can feel organic rather than machine-made.

Publisher Round Hill has filed separate copyright suits against Suno and Anthropic seeking up to $1bn each, with statutory damages of up to $150,000 per work willfully infringed. It says it isn't looking to settle — a counterweight to the wave of licensing deals.

OpenTune is a free, open-source AI pitch-correction tool for Windows and macOS — a Melodyne/Auto-Tune-style alternative built on a neural approach. Still in beta, and currently Chinese-only in the UI.

Warner Music CEO Robert Kyncl defended the label's Suno licensing deal on Semafor's Mixed Signals podcast while UMG and Sony press on with litigation: "In my opinion, you embrace it." A split in how majors are positioning generative music tools.

gesture.live is a free browser-based app from developer Robin van Soelen that turns a webcam into a gestural instrument via hand tracking. No hardware controller required — just a browser and a camera.

Both The American Dollar and Jamendo have abruptly dropped their copyright infringement lawsuits against Suno. The quiet dismissals hint at settlements reshaping the legal ground under AI music generation.

AI-assisted plugin development is redefining how music software gets made, and by whom. Developers describe shipping DSP tools without a traditional coding background — and what that does to the plugin market.

BMG and Suno have formed a "global alliance" promising new revenue streams for artists plus opt-in choice over whether their work trains or feeds generative AI. It also settles Suno's prior use of BMG recordings and publishing works.

Brian May asked an AI image generator to recreate Queen's The Game cover and was unimpressed: "So this is the kind of intelligence that will soon be ruling the world??!" A pointed test of generative tools against real music artwork.
